'''Michela Procesi''' (born 1973) is an Italian mathematician specializing in Hamiltonian [[partial differential equation]]s such as the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]] or [[wave equation]]. The [[Degasperis–Procesi equation]] is named for her.{{r|coclite}} She is a professor of mathematics at [[Roma Tre University]].

==Education and career==
Procesi was born in 1973 in Rome,{{r|cv|mad}} the daughter of mathematician [[Claudio Procesi]].{{r|mad}} She earned a [[laurea]] in physics at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]] in 1998, and continued at la Sapienza for a PhD in mathematics in 2002.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Estimates on Hamiltonian splittings: tree techniques in the theory of homoclinic splitting and Arnold diffusion for a-priori stable systems'', was supervised by [[Luigi Chierchia]].{{r|mg}}

She became a postdoctoral researcher at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] in [[Trieste]] and, with the support of the [[Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi]], at Roma Tre University.{{r|unina}} After continued work as a researcher at the [[University of Naples Federico II]] and la Sapienza, she obtained a position as an associate professor at Roma Tre University in 2015. She has been a full professor there since 2019.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Procesi was an invited speaker at the 2022 (virtual) [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|icm}}
